description:
Aggregate and browse AI coding agent sessions (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, etc.) in one place. Desktop app, self-hosted server, or Docker.

Codeg (Code Generation) is an enterprise-grade multi-agent coding workspace. It unifies local AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, OpenClaw, Cline, etc.) in a desktop app, standalone server, or Docker container — enabling remote development from any browser — with conversation aggregation, parallel git worktree development, MCP/Skills management, chat channel interactions (Telegram, Lark, iLink, etc.), and integrated Git/file/terminal workflows.
This release adds support for Claude Fable 5.2, updates Codex and several other agents, and fixes Qoder failing to start on Windows and MiniMax questions not showing as cards.
Improved
- Claude Code is updated to 2.1.321 with adapter 0.102.0, so the Fable model is now Fable 5.2, and a saved Fable 5.1 selection through an API gateway switches to Fable 5.2 automatically instead of falling back to the default model.
- Codex is updated to adapter 2.6.0 (Codex 0.166.0), and its async questions now display as answer cards that stay in sync during the conversation and in history.
- Grok background sub-agents show live progress after the turn that launched them ends. (#1109)
- Updated OpenCode to 2.2.6, CodeBuddy to 2.182.0, Qoder to 1.1.86, the ZCode bridge to 0.82.3 and Command Code to 1.88.5.
Fixed
- Qoder starts normally again on Windows, and its diagnostics show the actual program being launched or the reason it could not be found. (#1101 by @leehom0123)
- MiniMax questions to the user appear as interactive question cards instead of raw JSON, including each option's description. (#1111 by @xy3xy3)
- When a Codex conversation's model provider no longer matches, codeg shows a clear notice instead of silently starting an empty session that loses the history.
- Reopened Claude Code context compaction summaries no longer include internal prompt text meant for the model.
- OpenCode 2.2.6 conversation history displays its complete content.
Thanks to @leehom0123 (#1101) and @xy3xy3 (#1111) for their contributions, and to @momomomo820 (#1109) for the report.
